one_line: A master Indian Ocean shipwright-pilot who builds and navigates sewn-plank monsoon ships between Malabar, Gujarat and Oman.

appearance.age_look: mid-30s, lean and wiry from hard labour, with calloused hands and a sailor’s balanced stance
appearance.face: oval face with sun-browned medium-brown complexion, strong nose, sharp dark eyes, faint crow’s-feet, trimmed moustache and short beard; a small old scar on the left eyebrow; default expression is calm, alert focus with a hint of wry confidence
appearance.hair: thick black hair pulled back into a short knot at the back of the head, sides neatly kept; a plain off-white cotton headscarf (like a narrow turban band) wrapped once around the forehead and tied at the back, with a small red tilak mark just visible beneath the cloth
appearance.costume: A knee-length, long-sleeved cotton tunic (kurta) in muted indigo blue, slightly faded and sweat-darkened at seams, with side slits for movement; over it a sleeveless, waist-length brownish-red cotton vest reinforced with visible stitch lines and small coconut-fibre loops for holding tools; a simple undyed cotton dhoti wrapped firmly and brought between the legs, ending mid-calf, with a narrow dark-brown border; under it, bare-looking but fully covered calves and sturdy dark-brown leather sandals strapped around the ankles; around his waist a thick, twisted coir rope belt knotted at the side, from which hang a small bronze knife in a plain wooden sheath and a few wooden pegs; he wears a single small gold hoop earring in the left ear and a simple black-thread necklace with a tiny copper talisman, plus a narrow red-thread bracelet on his right wrist; fabrics look handwoven with subtle uneven texture, no flashy patterns beyond simple borders
appearance.signature: A well-used wooden caulking and stitching kit: a palm-sized curved wooden sewing awl with a polished handle, bundled together with a coil of brown coconut coir rope and a flat wooden caulking mallet, all bound by a thin coir cord and usually carried slung over his shoulder like a diagonal tool bandolier.

ref_desc: Samudra-Nayan is a sun-browned, sharp-eyed mid-30s shipwright-pilot with tied-back black hair under an off-white headscarf, wearing an indigo kurta, brownish-red vest, off-white dhoti, coir rope belt and sandals, carrying a wooden sewing awl with coir rope and caulking tools.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of Samudra-Nayan, a dignified Indian Ocean shipwright-pilot from the Malabar–Gujarat–Oman trade, shown front and three-quarter views: he is a lean mid-30s man with an oval, sun-browned medium-brown face, strong nose, sharp dark eyes with faint crow’s-feet, a small scar on his left eyebrow, trimmed moustache and short beard, and a calm, alert expression; his thick black hair is pulled into a short knot at the back and wrapped with a plain off-white cotton headscarf like a narrow turban band, a tiny red tilak mark just visible beneath; he wears a knee-length, long-sleeved muted indigo cotton kurta with side slits, a sleeveless brownish-red cotton vest reinforced with visible stitching and tool loops, and a firmly wrapped off-white cotton dhoti with a narrow dark-brown border reaching mid-calf, plus sturdy dark-brown leather sandals; around his waist is a thick coir rope belt holding a small bronze knife in a wooden sheath and a few wooden pegs, and he has a single small gold hoop earring in his left ear, a black-thread necklace with a tiny copper talisman, and a narrow red-thread bracelet on his right wrist; his signature prop is a wooden caulking and stitching kit—curved wooden sewing awl, coil of brown coconut coir rope, and flat wooden caulking mallet—bundled and slung diagonally over his shoulder like a tool bandolier; use a grounded palette of indigo blue, brownish red, off-white, dark brown and coconut-fibre brown, and emphasise practical, weathered textiles and tools suitable for sewn-plank monsoon ships.
